title: 100,000 Workers Protest Belgian Austerity Measures

image.attribution: William Murphy from Dublin, Ireland / Wikimedia Commons / CC-BY-SA-2.0

main_content:
At least 100,000 workers took to the streets of Brussels on Thursday to protest the Belgian government’s free-market reforms and austerity measures.

At least 14 people were injured when protesters clashed with the police.

Protesters pelted police with stones and fireworks, overturning cars or setting them on fire. Police used tear gas and water cannons to disperse the demonstrators.

The workers were protesting plans by the country’s new center-right government to increase the pension age from 65 to 67, freeze wages and cut public services.

The government says it must implement austerity measures to keep the budget deficit in line with European Union requirements. It also insists that businesses need more tax breaks to compete in the global market.

Trade unions have objected to the government plans, saying they undermine Belgium’s welfare state. The unions have announced they will push their demands forward during a several-week long campaign that will culminate in a general strike on December 15.

questions.question: Why did the workers protest?
options: They demanded better job opportunities for the youth.
They opposed the government's free-market reforms and austerity measures.
They supported the government's decision on pension reforms.
They were promoting a new trade agreement with the EU.
questions.answer: They opposed the government's free-market reforms and austerity measures.

questions.question: What did the protesters do during the clash with police?
options: They pelted police with stones and fireworks.
They used tear gas and water cannons.
They overturned police vehicles and blocked the streets peacefully.
They handed out flyers and held a sit-in.
questions.answer: They pelted police with stones and fireworks.

questions.question: What are the new government’s plans?
options: To increase minimum wage and improve healthcare services.
To freeze wages, cut public services, and raise the pension age.
To introduce new tax reforms for middle-class families.
To enhance public spending on infrastructure projects.
questions.answer: To freeze wages, cut public services, and raise the pension age.
